capability: Explain ELF LOAD ranges, zero-fill and declared page-permission unions without executing a binary.
user: Build and release engineers reviewing a small ELF handoff.
pain: Individual segment flags do not explain shared-page permission unions or overlapping virtual mappings.
contract: ELF32/64, little/big endian, identification/version1, EXEC/DYN, standard header/program-entry sizes and1..128 program headers. LOAD validates file/memory sizes, class address limits, known R/W/X flags and p_align congruence. Report backed/zero-fill intervals, overlap ambiguity, entry outside executable LOAD, W+X segments/stack and W+X page flag unions. Page-offset incongruence is a finding. Page size is a declared power of two512..65536, default4096; interval sweep avoids enumeration of huge virtual ranges. PT_INTERP is read as bounded ASCII but never opened/executed.
limits: 8 MiB. Other program-header kinds are ignored, section headers/relocations/ABI-specific semantics unverified. No loader simulation, ASLR, dynamic linking, DWARF, exploitation assessment or safety certificate. Missing GNU_STACK is unknown information, not a healthy-stack claim. Page union is a declared model; actual OS loading/permissions can differ.
acceptance: Both classes/endians, shared-page union, BSS, virtual overlap, entry failure, file/align rejection and huge virtual intervals without page allocation.
notes: LIEF parses and modifies broad executable formats; pyelftools and Goblin already expose ELF segments/flags and much more. Our evidence report is a narrow read-only workflow, not proof of an absent feature or a safer parser.
overlap: Filesystem POSIX ACL tooling and binary media tools do not model ELF virtual LOAD intervals. No owned ELF page-union inspector was found.
expected: Exit1 intentionally: separate RX/RW LOAD byte ranges share a4096-byte page, whose declared flag union is RWX; zero-fill ranges remain explicit.
